title: Access and Mobility Management Services; Stage 3 (AMF SBI)
tagline: AMF — access anchor that hands PDU sessions to SMF
summary: TS 29.518 defines the Namf services on the AMF. For PDU session establishment, the AMF is the access-side orchestrator: it receives the UE request over N1/N2, selects an SMF, and invokes Nsmf_PDUSession on SMF. It does not call Npcf_SMPolicyControl directly — session policy is SMF's responsibility after CreateSMContext.
defines: Namf_Communication — UE context, N1N2 message transfer, registration
PduSessionContext in UE context — tracks active PDU sessions per UE
whyItMatters: Every PDU session in 5G starts on the AMF. Without understanding 29.518, the handoff from radio access to session management (29.502) and the return path when SMF completes establishment are opaque. The 29.512 policy call happens inside SMF after AMF triggers PostSmContexts.

entryPoints.name: PDU Session Establishment Request
entryPoints.description: UE requests a new PDU session via NAS — AMF receives over N1.
AMF creates SM context on SMF — primary SBI trigger for PDU session on core.
SMF requests AMF to deliver N1/N2 signalling toward UE and RAN during session setup.

entryPoints.name: CreateSMPolicy
entryPoints.description: SMF requests session policy from PCF after AMF handoff — not an AMF SBI call.
